name: Strait of Khawr Sabah
inspired_by: The Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf littoral as of 2026: an arid Iranian coast of bare mountains, windcatcher port towns and mangrove creeks to the north; a fjord-cut limestone peninsula (Musandam type) and a flat, wealthy Arab Gulf coast with ports, oil and LNG terminals to the south; and small contested islands in the channel. Iran contested or closed the strait during the 2026 war. The channel is narrowed and all towns are fictional.
climate: Hot desert (Koppen BWh) with very high humidity on the coast. Summers 38-46 C with 60-90% humidity and heat index above 50 C; winters 15-25 C; rain under 150 mm, in a few winter storms that cause flash floods off the mountains.
seasons: Winter (Dec-Feb): pleasant, occasional storms and flash floods, shamal winds with rough seas
Spring (Mar-May): heating up, dust storms from the interior
Summer (Jun-Sep): extreme humid heat, haze, calm seas at dawn, sea fog some mornings
Autumn (Oct-Nov): cooling, clear air, fishing season

vegetation: none (water): shallow turquoise shelves near shore
almost bare limestone and ophiolite rock
acacia and Ziziphus spina-christi in gullies
Prosopis cineraria (ghaf) and Prosopis juliflora thickets

terrain.relief: Steep mountains drop straight into the sea on the peninsula (south-east) with deep drowned valleys (khors) and cliffs; the Iranian north coast has a narrow plain under bare ridges up to 1,400 m; the south-west is a flat coastal plain with sabkha. The channel between is 6-8 km wide and 40-60 m deep, with three small islands.
features: alluvial fans and wadis from the mountains
small islands with a lighthouse and a military post
dredged shipping lanes, breakwaters and reclaimed land
terrain.water: Sea covers roughly 40% of the map (channel and bays); no rivers; wadis flood briefly after storms; desalination supplies towns; wells and falaj-type channels feed old palm gardens.

generator.approach: Heightmap at 10 m including bathymetry (negative heights). A coastline mask defines land; the channel is a smoothed corridor carved to -40 to -60 m with shelves; khors are drowned ridged-noise valleys on the peninsula (land carved below sea level near the coast). Islands are cellular bumps in the channel.

noise_layers.purpose: peninsula and north-coast mountains, masked by distance from the flat south-west plain

generator.erosion: Thermal erosion only on mountains (capped 55 degrees: cliffs stay); hydraulic pass light, to cut wadis and build alluvial fans at the coast.
generator.rivers: None. Wadis from flow accumulation, dry except during storm events; drowned valleys (khors) placed by lowering terrain below sea level along ridged-noise troughs that meet the coast.
generator.settlement_flattening: Ports and industrial areas on reclaimed flat land at 2-4 m with straight quay edges; fishing villages on cove beaches flattened to 1-3 m; mountain villages per plot on terraces.
generator.notes: Naval traffic (tankers, dhows, fast boats) is a big part of the map and needs a sea-lane spline layer. AAVs and boats are key; boarding a ship is a POI built of STEEL structure voxels.

settlements.architecture: South-coast Gulf city district: walled two-storey villas in sand and white render with flat roofs and parapets, shaded courtyards and car ports; five- to fifteen-storey apartment and office towers with glass; malls; mosques with domes and pencil minarets; wide roads and roundabouts.
settlements.wall_class: Villa compound walls 25 cm block render medium; concrete frames thick; glass facades none.
layout_rules: corniche and marina on the shore
souq and old quarter near the creek
mall and towers on the main highway

settlements.architecture: North-coast Iranian port town: older houses of coral stone and gypsum plaster with windcatcher towers (badgir), wooden-latticed windows, narrow shaded lanes; newer two- to four-storey concrete and brick buildings; a fishing harbour, a bazaar, an IRGC Navy jetty.
settlements.wall_class: Coral stone 50-60 cm thick; newer brick 20 cm medium; concrete frames thick.
layout_rules: organic old core of lanes around a bazaar and a Friday mosque
newer grid on the edge, IRGC naval base fenced off on the shore

settlements.architecture: Fishing villages in coves and khors: one-storey stone and block houses with flat roofs, a small mosque, boat ramps, dhows and fiberglass skiffs, nets drying; some reachable only by boat. Mountain villages of stone houses and terraced plots.
settlements.wall_class: Stone houses thick; block houses thin.
layout_rules: on a cove beach between cliffs
boat ramp and fish market as the centre

settlements.architecture: Labour accommodation for migrant workers near industrial sites: rows of two- to three-storey prefab or block dormitory buildings, canteens, a fenced perimeter, bus parks.
settlements.wall_class: Prefabs very thin; block dorms thin.
layout_rules: gated, buses at shift change (05:00 and 18:00)
next to refineries and the port

settlements.architecture: Energy and military compounds: an oil export terminal with tank farms and jetties, an LNG plant with spherical tanks and flare stacks, a container port with cranes, a coastal naval base, an island garrison with bunkers, a fast-boat base in a khor with boat shelters cut into the cliffs.
settlements.footprint_m: tank 60 m diameter; terminal 1500x2000; boat base 300x400
settlements.wall_class: Tank walls steel (thin, hazard); concrete bunkers and boat shelters thick; berms thick.
layout_rules: on reclaimed land with straight quays
boat shelters at the foot of cliffs

infrastructure.roads: South: six-lane coastal highway, dual carriageways and roundabouts, a mountain road through tunnels and hairpins on the peninsula. North: a two-lane coastal road and tracks into the mountains. No road link across the strait.
infrastructure.rail: None (a freight spur into the container port is proposed).
infrastructure.power: Gas-fired power and desalination plants on both coasts; pylons along the highway.
infrastructure.ports: Container port and oil terminal (south), LNG jetties, fishing harbours, a naval base on each coast, a fast-boat base in a khor, dhow harbours.
infrastructure.airfields: One international airport on the south-west plain (out of bounds), one military airstrip on the north coast, helipads at terminals.
infrastructure.checkpoints: Port and terminal gates with vehicle scanners, coast-guard posts, IRGC checkpoints on the north coastal road, an island garrison controlling the channel.

conditions: shamal wind with rough seas and dust
rare winter thunderstorms with flash floods
weather.visibility_notes: Haze limits long-range optics to 3-8 km in summer; shamal days ground small boats and helicopters; strong glare off water and white buildings; heat drains stamina (proposed heat stress for heavy armour).
weather.dust_or_snow: Dust from the interior in spring and summer; no snow.

civilians.behaviour: City life shifts to early morning and after sunset in summer; malls and souqs busy in the evening; fishermen out before dawn; migrant workers commute by bus at shift changes; on attack alerts, residents shelter indoors and port workers evacuate to assembly points. Fishing skiffs and dhows crowd the channel and are easily mistaken for fast attack boats.
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: The sea is crowded with civilian boats; identification at sea is the main casualty risk. Labour camps and city districts are very dense.

factions_present.where: North coast and islands: IRGC Navy fast-boat bases in khors, island garrisons, coastal missile and drone sites, the port town; fast-boat swarms in the channel.
South-east peninsula and city: ports, naval base, terminal security, air defence.
LNG plant concession and the mediation venue on the south-west coast (fictional composite: Qatari-owned sites on this coast).
Oil export terminal concession on the south-west coast and patrol vessels.
Warships and helicopters in the channel, escort of tankers, the allied naval base.
Frigate and mine-countermeasure vessels in the channel; staff at the allied naval base.
European maritime-awareness mission frigate; base facilities on the south coast.
Escort frigate and boarding teams in the channel.
Frigate with the European escort mission.
Destroyer escorting Indian-flagged tankers through the channel.
Destroyer of the anti-piracy unit escorting Korean ships.
Patrol vessel escorting Pakistani shipping at the map's east edge.
Contracted security at ports and terminals for Gulf business clients; armed escort boats; competes for the same jobs.
Embarked security teams on tankers and VIP protection at the mediation venue.

frontline: A sea frontline. The channel's control state (open, contested, closed) is the main variable: Iranian escalation events raise fast-boat swarms, drone attacks on terminals and ship seizures, moving the channel to contested or closed; escort convoys, boarding successes and destroyed boat bases move it back toward open. Land zones on the north coast are Iranian and never flip; south-coast zones flip only in alert level. The war sim posts escort, counter-drone and ship-recovery contracts from Gulf and naval clients; rival PMCs bid on the same jobs and may sabotage the player's.
contract_hooks: Escort a tanker convoy through the channel against fast-boat harassment (clients are, qat, usa)
Retake a seized ship at anchor and recover the crew (clients are, gbr, usa)
Counter-drone defence of an oil terminal or LNG plant (clients sau, qat, are)
Port security sweep and container cache interdiction (client are)
VIP protection and hostage hand-over security at the mediation venue (client qat)
Anti-smuggling raid on a dhow harbour network (client are)
Recover a downed drone from an island reef under garrison observation (client usa)
Evacuate migrant workers from a labour camp after a strike (client are)

hot_zones.name: Strait channel and islands
hot_zones.layout: IRGC fast-boat base in a khor as HQ; island garrisons and a coastal missile site as 3-4 outposts; patrol boat 'checkpoints' on the lanes; roaming fast-boat pairs; 1 QRF (boat swarm) at the base. Player operates by boat, helicopter and LHD.

insertion.fob: LHD offshore in the south of the channel is the primary base (helicopters, boats, AAVs). An optional FOB at the allied naval base on the south coast for land contracts.

early_game_notes: The main threat is a state navy and missile force (irn, mid) plus rival PMCs (mid); Gulf client port-security jobs can be offered early as low-intensity work.
ambient_audio: call to prayer over the water
proposed: channel control state (open/contested/closed) as the frontline variable
qat and sau presence as site concessions on a fictional composite coast
